summary:
Clean. Since 0ca9f0c the only code change is the class summary of `tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/WindowScriptParseTests.cs`, lines 8-13; no code changed. The full default suite passes 374/374 and the edited file has no bytes of 0x80 or above.

I checked the new summary's claims under Windows PowerShell 5.1 on scratch files saved as UTF-8 without a byte-order mark:
- **Holds:** "catches only non-ASCII that 5.1 decodes into a quote character".
- **Holds:** "an e with an acute accent in the same place gave none".
- **Holds:** "a curly quote or dash in a comment gave none".
- **Wrong:** "a curly quote or dash inside a double-quoted string gave 5.1 two parse errors". Only the dashes do. An em dash or en dash in a double-quoted string gave errors=2, but curly double quotes (U+201C/U+201D) and a curly apostrophe (U+2019) there each gave errors=0. Their UTF-8 bytes (E2 80 9C/9D/99) contain none of cp1252's quote bytes 0x91-0x94. The summary also credits this to the SL-059 review, which only measured a dash in a string.

`WindowCasesIsAscii` still rejects every byte of 0x80 or above, so no input goes unchecked. The wrong example is a record-accuracy note, so I put it in drift and did not file it as a finding.

O-006 is still owed to validate-slice and needs a person with a second sign-in session.

Second round: Nothing new this round; the review stays clean.

The only change since 0ca9f0c is prose: lines 8-13 of the class summary in `tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/WindowScriptParseTests.cs`. It adds no parser, matcher, reader, boundary or error path. The code this diff reaches was already tested adversarially in earlier rounds, and nothing in it has changed:
- `WindowCasesIsAscii`: BOMs, an empty file, a missing file, a lone CR and UTF-16 input.
- `WindowCasesParses`: a missing file (exits 1 under both hosts) and quoting of the path.
- `RigLockScopeWordingTests`: file types, reparse points, the `bin`/`obj` filter and line splitting.
- The Fitness patterns: CRLF, and `(?mi)` with `[^\n]*`.

The one inaccuracy in the new prose has not changed since the first round and is already in drift. It is the "curly quote" example at lines 9-10: I measured errors=0 under 5.1, and it has no effect on behaviour.

The full suite passes 374/374. O-006 is still owed to validate-slice and needs a person with a second sign-in session.

`WindowScriptParseTests.WindowCasesParses` passes under powershell.exe (Desktop) and pwsh.exe (Core) in the 374/374 run.
The SmbRigTests pass in the full suite, and `RigLock.Take` is unchanged.
`SmbRig.cs:176` still holds the byte-identical literal `Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig`, and its only reference is `SmbRig.cs:51`.
It needs a second sign-in session, which the agent sandbox cannot create (spike 1). It is still owed to validate-slice, and a person has to run it.
`WindowScriptParseTests.cs:19-32` (`WindowCasesIsAscii`) is unchanged: it rejects a UTF-8 byte-order mark and any byte of 0x80 or above. The summary no longer claims the parse check covers comments.

cases.evidence: Covered by a command, not a test: StallRig builds outside the .slnx, and its csproj links `SmbRig.cs`.
The parse Theory runs under 5.1 and pwsh, and `WindowCasesIsAscii` guards every byte, including comments.
`RigLockScopeWordingTests` asserts DoesNotMatch on the real unrelated lines and scans the real files.
The 18 SmbRigTests pass with GUID-suffixed lock names, and `Take` is unchanged.
Deferred, and the reason still holds: the lock is still `Local\`, and the sandbox still refuses Register-ScheduledTask (spike 1).

drift: The summary at `tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/WindowScriptParseTests.cs:9-10` says "a curly quote or dash inside a double-quoted string gave 5.1 two parse errors (SL-059 review)". Under powershell.exe 5.1.26100.9444, with UTF-8 no-BOM scratch files, only the em dash and en dash gave errors=2. Curly double quotes (U+201C/U+201D) and a curly apostrophe (U+2019) in a double-quoted string gave errors=0, because their UTF-8 bytes contain no cp1252 quote byte (0x91-0x94). The SL-059 review measured only a dash in a string. The fix is to drop "a curly quote or" from line 9. It has no effect on behaviour, because `WindowCasesIsAscii` rejects every byte of 0x80 or above.

Still true from the earlier review: the design gives the doc as `docs/SL-020-scanner.md`, which does not exist, and the builder edited `docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md` without noting the difference. The settled `WindowCases.ps1` rule in `.taad/fitness.yaml` and `RigLockScopeWordingTests.Claim` are the same regex written twice, and nothing checks that the two copies agree. The default suite now needs pwsh.exe on PATH. `WindowCasesIsAscii` makes ASCII-only a standing rule for every future edit of `WindowCases.ps1`, not just this slice's edit.
